notes: inherent: The inherent vowel is a. It is not said at the end of a word (ગુજરાત gujarat, ઘર ghar), and people rarely type it there; after a final cluster it is typed about as often as not (મિત્ર mitra / mitr, શબ્દ shabd / shabda). Inside a word Gujarati drops it between a vowel + lone consonant and a lone consonant + vowel (કરવું karvu, ગુજરાતી gujrati), and people type it either way, so the weighted tables have schwaDeleted. The pack's format-1 walk has no schwa rule and keeps every medial a (કરવું karavun); the skeleton drops an a between consonants instead, on both sides. anusvara: ં is n inside a word, and m before a labial (સંબંધ sambandh): the skeleton folds mb and mp to nb and np. At the end of a word, where it marks the neuter and the locative (કરવું, સારું, શું, ઘરમાં), chat usually leaves it out (karvu, saru, shu, gharma) and careful typists write n or m (karvun, gharmam); the skeleton drops a final n or m after a vowel (dropTrailing), so all three are one key. The price: a word that really ends in n or m shares its key with the word without it (નામ with ના). m is not listed as a spelling of ં, though Aksharantar's annotators type it at the end of a word more than n: the tables have one list for ં wherever it stands, the fit would make m its canonical spelling, and the key of every word with ં inside would then have m where people type n. The transliterator still learns the final m from Aksharantar's mined pairs. e: એ is e; Aksharantar's annotators also typed ey and ay (meynipyuleyshans), which are kept as rare spellings for the transliterator; the skeleton folds ey and ay to e (not ae: the ergative એ after આ, છોકરાએ chhokarae, is two vowels). ay is also the end of થાય, સમય, વિજય, which so share keys with words in e (thay with the); it is folded because one in twelve calibration pairs is typed that way. vowels: ઇ and ઈ are both i, ઉ and ઊ both u; long ones are sometimes typed ee and oo, and આ as aa. The skeleton folds aa, ee, ii, oo, uu. letters: છ is chh or ch (છે chhe / che), ઝ jh or z, ફ f or ph, વ v or w, શ sh or s (શું shu / su), ળ l. ઋ and ૃ are ru in Gujarati (કૃષ્ણ krushna) as often as ri. ક્ષ is ksh, જ્ઞ gn or gy, ત્ર tr, શ્ર shr. skeleton: A final n or m after a vowel is dropped first (dropTrailing), so karvun, karvum and karvu are one key: the neuter anusvara at the end of a word is typed all three ways. An a between two consonants is dropped (dropBetweenConsonants), so the medial inherent vowel typed or not gives one key (karvu / karavu, gujrati / gujarati). chh and ch fold to c, sh to s, the aspirates to their plain stops, f and ph to p, z and jh to j, w to v. A final a after a consonant is dropped, which covers the final inherent vowel typed or not.
